claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens contain realistic lattice defects and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
A machine-learning-enhanced interatomic potential can be calibrated using DFT and molecular-dynamics data for this alloy.
The proposed potential embeds temperature-dependent phonon interactions.
The proposed potential explicitly embeds lattice-defect and oxygen-impurity scattering mechanisms.
Transport measurements are available for HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen across nearly 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Lattice defects and oxygen impurities act as scattering centers in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen impurities and other defects perturb the electronic density of states.
Oxygen impurities and other defects perturb phonon-transport pathways.
Explicit defect modeling enables the approach to adjust effective electron-scattering rates.
Explicit defect modeling enables the approach to adjust effective phonon-scattering rates.
Capturing defect-dependent scattering will reproduce temperature-dependent departures from perfect-crystal behavior.
The ML-enhanced approach will predict electrical conductivity more accurately than conventional defect-free analytical models.
The conductivity predictions will agree with experiment within approximately 15% in both specified temperature regimes.
Conventional analytical models neglect relevant defects and produce larger conductivity discrepancies.
The proposed method will improve on conventional defect-free models by approximately 20% or more.
The claimed applicability is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr near 0–200 K and 300–1200 K with oxygen content around 1 wt.%.
Validity outside the specified temperature intervals or at substantially different oxygen levels is untested.
Existing data do not fully constrain defect characterization and oxygen scattering at very low temperatures.
Failure to attain a 15% conductivity-error margin or at least approximately 20% improvement over the baseline will falsify the hypothesis.
